URmessage - closed alpha
========================

Thank you for testing. This is an early build on a live network. Please read the
two short warnings at the bottom before you send anything you would mind losing.


WHAT YOU NEED
-------------

  1. This folder, unzipped anywhere you like. Nothing is installed and nothing
     is written outside your own user folder.
  2. A credential file, sent to you separately. It is named like
     "tester3.jwt" and it is yours alone - it is the key to your account, so
     treat it the way you would treat a password.


SETTING IT UP (once)
--------------------

  If you tested an earlier build of URmessage on this computer, do this first:
  the test network was emptied for this build, and this build cannot use the
  data an earlier one saved (it would tell you "This installation cannot make a
  join code"). Press Windows+R, paste this, and press Enter:

         %LOCALAPPDATA%\URmessage\app

  In the folder that opens, delete the folder called "live". Leave the folder
  %LOCALAPPDATA%\URmessage\dev alone: your credential is in it.

  1. Press Windows+R, paste this, and press Enter:

         %LOCALAPPDATA%\URmessage\dev

     If the folder does not exist, create it: go to %LOCALAPPDATA%, make a
     folder called URmessage, and a folder called dev inside it.

  2. Copy your credential file into that folder and RENAME it to exactly:

         user1.jwt

     (Yes, "user1" even though you may be tester 3. The name is what this build
     looks for. It will be your own name in a later one.)

     If you would rather keep the file somewhere else, set the environment
     variable URMESSAGE_LIVE_JWT to the file's full path, and the app reads that
     file instead.

  3. Run URmessage.exe from this folder.

If the app says "URmessage needs its credential", the file is not where it
looked: the message names the exact folder and file name it expects.


GETTING INTO A CONVERSATION
---------------------------

There are two ways in, and the box the app shows you offers both. If somebody
has already made the group, use the first. If you are the one making it, use the
second.

The first time you run it, the app connects and then shows a box called
"Join a group". That takes a few seconds: by default URmessage reaches its
server through URnetwork (see YOUR IP ADDRESS below) and has to pick a way out
first. You do not need to do anything while it says it is connecting.

When the box appears:

  1. Press "Copy join code". That puts a long line of text on your clipboard.
  2. Send it to whoever invited you to this test, any way you like - email,
     Signal, a message. It is NOT a secret: all it lets somebody do is add this
     computer to a group.
  3. They will send you back an INVITATION, which is a longer line of text.
     Keep it private: it is made for this computer's join code, so it only
     works here, and only once. Do not post it anywhere, and do not forward it.
  4. Paste the invitation into the second box and press "Join".

The box closes itself and the conversation appears. After that the app just
opens into it.

If the invitation is refused, the message under the box says why in plain
words, and what to do next:

  * If it asks for a new join code, press "Make a new join code", send the new
    code, and ask for a fresh invitation.
  * If it says your join code is still good, do not make a new one: do what the
    message says.
  * If it says this computer still holds an old copy of the group, press "Leave
    the old copy", and then use the same invitation again.


MAKING THE GROUP YOURSELF
-------------------------

Press "Start a new group instead".

It is made at once, and it is NOT usable yet - it has only you in it, nothing
can be sent, and the app says so. A group opens when its first other member is
added. So:

  1. Ask somebody for their join code (they press "Copy join code" in their own
     URmessage and send you what it gives them).
  2. Paste it into the box and press "Add them to the group".
  3. The app shows you an INVITATION. Press "Copy invitation" and send it to
     that one person. Only their computer can open it, and it works once. Send
     it privately.
  4. Repeat 1-3 for each further person. The invitation shown is always for the
     code you just pasted - copy it before you add the next person.

If adding somebody is refused, the message says why in plain words, and what to
do next.

Press "Done" when you have finished adding people. You can send messages as
soon as the first person has joined.


YOUR IP ADDRESS
---------------

By default URmessage does not connect to its message server directly. It
connects through URnetwork: your encrypted traffic leaves the network through
another URnetwork connection, called an exit, and the message server only ever
sees the exit's address, never yours. The exit can see that something is
talking to the message server, but not what, and it never learns your address
either.

You can turn this off in Settings > Privacy and security > "Route through
URnetwork". It takes effect the next time you start the app. With it off, the
app connects directly. That can help if the network is struggling, but the
message server then sees your IP address.

Either way, the app checks the server's own key before it sends anything, so
nobody in between can pretend to be the server.


WHAT WORKS, AND WHAT DOES NOT
-----------------------------

Works: sending and receiving messages, replying to a message, reactions, the
member list with everyone's role, and - if you are an owner or an admin -
changing somebody's role or removing them from the group. In a group of
three or more, every message shows who sent it. Deleting your own messages
and leaving a conversation work too, and so does joining a conversation again
after you left it: see DELETING below.

Does NOT work yet, and the app says so on screen rather than pretending:

  * NAMES. There is no identity layer yet, so the app cannot know anybody's
    name and shows "unavailable". You CAN give each person a name that only
    you see: in the panel on the right, open a member and press "Name them".
    You can name a conversation the same way. These names stay on your
    computer and are never sent - nobody else, and not the server, sees them.
  * DELIVERY AND READ RECEIPTS. Nothing reports them, so your own messages stop
    at "Sent" and never go further. That is the truth, not a bug.
  * TELLING THE OTHERS YOU LEFT. Leaving is silent for now: see DELETING.
  * ATTACHMENTS, voice, video, and disappearing messages.
  * VERY LONG MESSAGES. A message can be about 65,000 bytes (a few hundred
    pages of plain text; fewer characters if you use emoji or non-Latin
    scripts). Past that, the Send button goes dark and the app tells you by
    how much. Your text stays in the box.

Anywhere the app cannot tell you something, it says "unavailable" rather than
inventing it. If you ever see it claim something it should not know, that is a
bug worth reporting and we would like to hear about it.


DELETING
--------

  * ONE MESSAGE. Hover over a message you sent and press the bin icon beside
    Reply and React. It is deleted for everyone, however old it is, and
    everybody sees "This message was deleted." in its place, so nobody can
    quietly rewrite a conversation. It reaches every device that is online
    and honest; anybody who already read it may have kept a copy, and
    nothing can detect that.
  * EVERY MESSAGE YOU SENT in a conversation: in the panel on the right,
    press "Delete all my messages". Only the messages this computer sent are
    deleted; everybody else's stay.
  * THE WHOLE CONVERSATION, FOR YOU: in the panel on the right, press "Delete
    for me and leave". It is deleted from THIS computer and the app goes back
    to the "Join a group" box. The others are NOT told. They keep their
    copies, including your messages unless you deleted those first, and you
    stay on their member list until they remove you. If you own the
    conversation, it is handed to the other person first, in the same step.
  * THE WHOLE CONVERSATION, FOR BOTH OF YOU: each of you presses "Delete all
    my messages" and then "Delete for me and leave".


TWO WARNINGS, AND THEY ARE REAL
-------------------------------

  1. DO NOT RUN TWO COPIES under the same credential - not on two computers,
     and not by copying your %LOCALAPPDATA%\URmessage folder to another
     machine. Two copies of one identity break the encryption for everything
     that identity sends. One credential, one computer.

  2. THIS IS AN ALPHA ON A TEST NETWORK. Messages may be lost, the group may
     need to be rebuilt, and the whole thing may be wiped between rounds.
     Please do not put anything in it that you would be upset to lose or to
     have read by somebody running the server.


IF SOMETHING GOES WRONG
-----------------------

There is a log at:

    %LOCALAPPDATA%\URmessage\app\logs\urmessage-app.log

It contains no message text and no credentials - it is safe to send on. Sending
it with a note about what you were doing is the single most useful thing you can
give us.
